forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Harrow pension board met twice in 2025-26, leaving two scheduled meetings inquorate and a compliance review incomplete
news_drafts.lead: Harrow Council's Pension Board met only twice in 2025-26, leaving two scheduled meetings inquorate and unable to proceed. As a result, a required review of the fund's compliance with the Pensions Regulator's Code of Practice remains incomplete. The regulator expects Local Government Pension Scheme boards to meet four times a year. The council has now filled a vacant board position for 2026-27, meaning all seats are occupied. Board members said the quorum failures were disappointing. The board also expressed concern about the performance of some investment managers against their benchmarks and noted that the pension administration team, after losing key personnel, has undergone restructuring with training plans in place for 2025-26.
news_drafts.paper_title: 2.0 Pension Board - Draft Pension Board Annual Report 2025-26, 30/07/2026 Pension Board

news_drafts.headline: Harrow forecasts £54.181m high needs deficit at year-end; government backs 90% of £29.570m to date
news_drafts.lead:
Harrow Council expects its deficit on high needs funding to rise from £29.570m to £54.181m by the end of 2026-27, according to the first-quarter budget monitoring report (the in-year check of spending against budget) that went to Cabinet on 24 September. High needs is the part of the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, which pays for children with special educational needs and disabilities.

The forecast increase of £24.611m was recorded in the first quarter of the year alone. The opening figure is the accumulated deficit at 31 March 2026.

The government has confirmed it will support up to 90% of that accumulated deficit, which is £26.613m, through a High Needs Stability grant. The paper says this is "subject to approval of a local SEND reform plan", with SEND meaning special educational needs and disabilities. The council would be responsible for the remaining 10%, or £2.957m. For deficits arising from 2026-27 onwards, the government has described an "appropriate and proportionate approach", but the paper says the detail has not yet been confirmed.

findings.paper_title: 2.1 Appx 1 Draft Annual Report of the Pension Board 25-26, 30/07/2026 Pension Board
findings.headline: The Board has expressed concern about the investment performance of some appointed fund managers relative to their benchmarks.
findings.detail: The Board is concerned about the relative performance of some investment managers and has asked that the Pension Fund Committee push managers (through the London Collective Investment Vehicle and otherwise) to improve performance against their benchmarks.
findings.matters: Underperformance of the pension fund increases the employer's (council's) future contribution requirements, raising budget obligations.
findings.figures: Specific performance gaps not quantified in report
findings.quote: We have expressed concern about the relative performance of some of the appointed investment managers and continue to ask that the Pension Fund Committee push investment managers, whether through the LCIV or otherwise, to improve performance against their benchmarks.

findings.paper_title: 2.1 Appx 1 Draft Annual Report of the Pension Board 25-26, 30/07/2026 Pension Board
findings.headline: The pension administration team has lost key personnel and struggled to meet performance standards, with restructuring and training plans now in place.
findings.detail: The Board expressed concern about administration team performance measured through KPIs. After losing key personnel, the team struggled to meet expectations. The administration team has undergone significant restructuring, including creation of a new pensions administration manager role, with training plans implemented for 2025-26. The Board will continue to monitor.
findings.matters: Failures in pension administration (missed deadlines, processing errors, regulatory breaches) could trigger enforcement action and financial penalties.
findings.figures: New pensions administration manager role created; team restructured
findings.quote: after the loss of key personnel the team has struggled to meet KPI expectations. The team has undergone significant restructuring and training plans have been put in place to improve the resilience and the performance of the team in 2025-26.

findings.paper_title: 2.1 Appx 1 Draft Annual Report of the Pension Board 25-26, 30/07/2026 Pension Board
findings.headline: The Board has not completed a required review of the fund's compliance with the Pensions Regulator's Code of Practice due to insufficient meetings.
findings.detail: The Board was asked to consider the outputs of a review into compliance with the Pensions Regulator's Code of Practice. The Board met only twice in 2025-26 (31 July 2025 and 4 November 2025), preventing this review from happening. The Pension Regulator expects LGPS Pension Boards to meet four times per year.
findings.matters: Failure to complete a required compliance review leaves the council exposed to unidentified regulatory risks and potential enforcement action by the Pensions Regulator.
findings.quote: The committee asked the board to consider in detail the outputs of the review into the fund's compliance with the Pensions Regulators Code of Practise and the failure to hold two meetings since November 2025 has meant this has not happened.

findings.paper_title: Recommendation to Council - Pension Board - 30 July 26
findings.headline: Vacant Pension Board position filled for 2026-27, all seats now occupied
findings.detail: The previously vacant position on the Pension Board has been filled for the 2026-27 municipal year, meaning all board seats are now filled. This directly addresses the cause of the prior year's quorum failures.
findings.matters: Full board capacity should enable completion of delayed compliance work and improve pension fund governance oversight going forward
findings.quote: The vacant position on the Pension Board had been filled for the 2026-27 Municipal Year, which meant that the Board had all seats filled for 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Recommendation to Council - Pension Board - 30 July 26
findings.headline: Pension Board only met twice in the year; two scheduled meetings failed due to quorum issues, leaving compliance review work incomplete
findings.detail: The Pension Board held only two meetings due to two scheduled meetings being inquorate and unable to proceed. Board members noted this was disappointing. As a result, a compliance review relating to the general code of practice that had been delegated to the Pension Board remains incomplete.
findings.matters: Governance failures in pension fund administration indicate weakness in the council's oversight of its significant pension liabilities
findings.figures: Board met only twice; two meetings were inquorate
findings.quote: The Board had only met twice; two meetings were inquorate and therefore unable to proceed. Board Members commented that this was disappointing.
